answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to post a bond in a scarce, transferable token, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fabricated work or collusive endorsements. Auditors are randomly assigned and paid from fees, while appeals require evidence and another bond, so creating many accounts does not multiply influence for free. A sybil attacker must lock up real capital for every identity and risks losing it; the ivory meadow and falcon labels can decorate profiles, but cannot substitute for bonded stake.
